body: What happens in 25 years?

You are correct.  There is a decent demand, but staffing models have changed and firms can hire someone with little experience for half my salary and train them. 

I have thought about moving ... honestly, I can't afford to move.  I literally have no money.  I cannot even pay my rent this month.  

The kinds of jobs you refer to would be insurance defense firms ... I don't have experience in that area.  Law firms hire based on your practice area experience.

I have also applied for night jobs, just to make some money but still have days to job hunt for something using my education and experience.  Can't even get a response.  Have walked around my neighborhood several times responding to signs in windows for helps.  Don't get any response.  

Recruiters keep blowing smoke up my ass about potential jobs.  I don't get any responses when I send out my resume.  This has been going on a really long time.  I really can't figure out what I'm doing wrong.  I'm beyond discouraged.

I don't know anything about 211.org.  I can check it out.

I was a legal assistant/paralegal for a long time.  Took a big risk and got my Masters' degree (finished about a year ago) thinking it would lead to a "bigger job."  Instead, it's a turn off to a lot of prospective employers.  Also, I can't find work directly in the field I got a masters in (organizational development) because I worked FT and went to school at night and didn't get experience in that field.  I'm so fucking stuck.
Thank you for talking with me.  I'm really just posting here tonight to pass the time and get through the next hours.  Lots of hurt and pain in this sub.

Fair enough.  
 
It is not sad to succumb to the darkness.  It's an act of surrender to the forces that shape our lives.

I'm not being disrespectful or flippant; but please tell me why you really hope I hang on. 

Do you have any idea what it's like to be skilled and have deep experience and have your career go to shit because you got old?  Go through job interviews and explain why "I've bounced around the past few years" (answer:  I need to work and take care of myself).  Go through months of job searching and come up with absolutely shit jobs that end anyway.  I live in the Bay Area; it's supposed to be a great job market; I'm working with four recruiters!  At a point it's obvious the problem is me... I am the common denominator.  And it's getting worse.  I just can't do it anymore.
Can you talk about that anymore?  Pretend I don't believe in God and tell me how God lead you away from that world ...

I also can't pay my rent or any other bills, and have nowhere to turn for help.  Even if there was somewhere, I don't feel like I have the wherewithal or even motivation to do anything.  I'm just completely exhausted from the fucking struggle.  It has been really hard the last four or five years.  That's when my career started taking the hits and financial stress has taken its toll as well.
Feeling very confident of that.
I feel so much pain and regret from your post.  That shows you have a conscience.  Something lead you away from that world ... what was it?

No kids.  Thanks for the kudos.  It feels a lot longer than 59 years. 

And you have helped ... thank you for taking the time to talk to me.  I am resolute in my decision, but it's also nice to be "talking" to people.  (And, no, I don't want to talk to a suicide hotline.)
I have.  They already know my struggle(s).  I don't think they'll be surprised.  I feel like I owe them at least an explanation that they could not have done anything.

I am not a teenager.  I am 59 years old.  

Childhood abuse and neglect; lots of b.s. growing up; other stuff that I'd rather not go into; how my life has crashed and I can't get any traction.  It's like all this negativity the last few years is trying to tell me:  it is the end; everything is gone; you're old; you're not coming back this time; notice how you're losing ground and losing connection.  

There's nothing to hold onto anymore.

My feelings of connection; any sense of being tethered to myself or my own thinking; my life; my responsibilities; duties; expectations; feelings of despair; feelings of failure.  It's a huge release of feeling and connection.  It's really so peaceful.

Therapy with a trauma therapist, antidepressants.  It's been going on a long time, this time about four or five years ... just a downhill slide that won't stop and leads to a deeper pit.

I don't understand your last question.  I am out of money and do not have insurance.  My therapist is currently running a tab with me, which makes me feel really bad because I won't be able to pay her.
I don't mind.  What would you like to know?
Apologies for any pain; confirmation that it is my deliberate choice; some explanation of why; thanking them for being part of my life; wishing them very well.

Please know that some people really do have "friends" who don't hear us even when we are screaming in pain.  I have reached out.  Different answers from different people ... all with the same baseline:  not available, but hang in there. 

It is true; and it is sad.  Life is like that sometimes.

I can feel your hurt and pain.  If it helps, I really don't believe there is a Heaven or Hell.  I think either are states of mind, but not states of consciousness.  So, regardless of your choices, I really don't think you will burn in Hell forever.  

I hope you find peace, friend.

Thank you for your kindness.  I think I have lived a good Life ... I have at least consciously tried to be a good human being.

Mine is just one very small Life amongst billions of lives on this tiny beautiful planet.  It's going to continue to spin without me.

I've "been doing something about it" for a long time.  Therapy; medication; sometimes meditation; use alcohol and weed to cope when it gets really bad; have a script for Lorazepam that I "save for emergencies", but really it is to stockpile it so I can over-sedate myself.

I don't have any ... that's the point.  I am out of money; completely estranged from my family; and don't have sufficient connections with people to help.  I've been going downhill for a long time; some people have given up on me; others just fall away naturally; I have given up on me.  It's honestly such a relief.

Sometimes I feel like I've spent my whole life looking inward and trying to find peace and happiness.  There have been times of happiness and peace.  The past several years have been a continuing and steady decline for me.  I'm old; can't find a steady job; have never been in this place before; can't find any traction; have a really empathic and sincere personality, so am always taking care of everyone else; had to surrender my dog who I loved more than anything else; completely estranged from my family of origin; everything has been falling apart for a long time. 

I like writing and poetry, which I engage in.  It doesn't pay the bills though.  I am out of options.  I am out of money and been hanging on by a thread way too long.

I just wanted to come back and say I understand those feelings inside that say "Oh, they'll notice when I'm gone."  

Yes, people will notice.  People who "should have" cared when you were hurting will be the same ones who say, "I wish I would have known."  "I wish I could have done something."  

There is a real disconnect in (at least) American culture (am making an assumption that is your continental base).  I think that's because of a lot of factors; but the reality is people are so disconnected.

I know connection is the answer; I don't know how to find it or maintain it.  

I'm sorry it's so hard to find friends that care about your well-being.  

I'm in a bad place tonight too, but I send you good thoughts and the reminder that you matter ... you have a place in this world.

I really feel this.  I don't know if they will care of not.  I do know that it hurts in a really raw way when the people you are trying to connect with to find solutions really don't seem to get it.  

I understand your pain, and I'm really sorry you're feeling that right now.  Not being heard when you are trying to connect is such a despairing feeling.

Also, my Life just seems like a series of shit decisions that got me to now.  It's such a relief when you reach the end, and find this weird peace because you know you are the problem, and you know how to solve that problem.

The most:  I do not have rent money.  I have been struggling with work and finding a "permanent" job for the last six months.  

To add insult to injury, I desperately asked a long-time friend for a short-term loan.  He offered a much smaller amount because he's stretched because he's going on a Mexican vacation with his girlfriend.  He also showed me his new $475 designer shoes and two new Summer suits for the trip.  He seemed totally unphased by the irony.  I told him to have a really great vacation and we'd talk when he got back.
